world.title: European allies rehearse postwar Ukraine force deployment in Poland
world.summary: France and Britain will lead 2,800 troops from 10 European countries in Koalicja, the first exercise for the Multinational Force-Ukraine (MNF-U), from Nov. 9 to 22 in southeastern Poland. The force is intended to support Ukraine only after a ceasefire by helping rebuild its armed forces, secure its airspace and restore
world.content: France and Britain will lead 2,800 troops from 10 European countries in Koalicja, the first exercise for the Multinational Force-Ukraine (MNF-U), from Nov. 9 to 22 in southeastern Poland. The force is intended to support Ukraine only after a ceasefire by helping rebuild its armed forces, secure its airspace and restore economic activity in the Black Sea. The land and air drills around Nowa Deba will test deployment, supply and coordination among national contingents. Turkey will lead a separate maritime simulation from Istanbul to prepare for possible mine-clearing in the Black Sea. The force is not a NATO operation and is not intended for offensive action, peacekeeping or ceasefire monitoring. Organizers say the Polish exercise will use light equipment rather than tanks. Any deployment remains conditional on a ceasefire and decisions by participating governments. The force’s eventual size and rules for responding to attacks on its troops remain unsettled. Russia opposes foreign troops in Ukraine.

world.title: Hackers breach Ukrainian and Russian alert apps with fake nuclear warnings
world.summary: Ukraine and Russia said hackers breached their civilian emergency-alert apps overnight Nov. 1-2, sending false warnings of radiation, chemical attacks, street fighting and nuclear strikes. Ukraine’s Air Force said there was no radiation threat; Russia’s Emergencies Ministry said a fabricated alert reached users in 33 r
world.content: Ukraine and Russia said hackers breached their civilian emergency-alert apps overnight Nov. 1-2, sending false warnings of radiation, chemical attacks, street fighting and nuclear strikes. Ukraine’s Air Force said there was no radiation threat; Russia’s Emergencies Ministry said a fabricated alert reached users in 33 regions. One Ukrainian message falsely claimed a Russian Oreshnik missile was incoming, while the Russian alert told people nuclear warheads had been launched and advised them to shelter in basements and stock up on food. Ukraine temporarily disabled its Air Alert app and warned users not to click links in suspicious notifications. The Russian ministry said attackers exploited a vulnerability in its app’s administrative panel, but other public warning channels—including SMS, broadcasts and sirens—continued to operate. Ukraine said the breach did not affect military command or security operations. The attackers’ identities and any connection between the two incidents have not been established. Ukraine’s Air Force accused Russia of hostile interference; Russian officials did not name a perpetrator, and a hacking group’s claim of responsibility was not independently verified. Ukraine’s app was reported restored overnight, while Russia’s ministry said it had identified the vulnerability the attackers exploited and was working to restore its app.
world.image_alt: Hackers breach Ukrainian and Russian alert apps with fake nuclear warnings

world.title: US sets Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi for November 10-11
world.summary: U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said Washington will mediate working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11. The agenda includes postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and steps toward ending the war. A senior U.S. official said Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Preside
world.content: U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said Washington will mediate working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11. The agenda includes postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and steps toward ending the war. A senior U.S. official said Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. negotiator, are expected to represent Washington. Before the Abu Dhabi meeting, U.S. negotiators plan to meet in Brussels this week with representatives of France, Germany, Britain, the European Union and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe’s future security framework and reconstruction support. Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to another round after meeting Witkoff in St. Petersburg, the U.S. official said. The last U.S.-mediated peace talks took place in February; Ukraine and Russia remain far apart on the terms of a possible settlement. Washington is seeking a breakthrough before winter, with the Abu Dhabi talks scheduled to begin Nov. 10.
world.image_alt: US sets Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi for November 10-11

world.title: Trump moves to end AGOA duty-free access for South Africa, Rwanda
world.summary: President Donald Trump has notified Congress and the governments of South Africa and Rwanda that he plans to end their eligibility under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), removing their duty-free access to the U.S. market from Jan. 1, 2027. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review fou
world.content: President Donald Trump has notified Congress and the governments of South Africa and Rwanda that he plans to end their eligibility under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), removing their duty-free access to the U.S. market from Jan. 1, 2027. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review found practices inconsistent with the program’s eligibility rules, including trade and investment barriers and threats to U.S. security and foreign-policy interests. Washington also cited corruption in South Africa and concerns about human rights, the rule of law and workers’ rights in Rwanda. The announcement gave no specific examples of the alleged violations. South Africa, AGOA’s largest beneficiary, exported about $1.7 billion in goods under the program in 2025, including vehicle parts, citrus and wine. Pretoria says those exports account for about 10% of its shipments to the U.S. and 1% of its global exports. It says it will support affected industries while seeking other markets. Washington is also increasing pressure on Rwanda over its alleged support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo; Rwanda denies backing the group. The planned exclusions carry a 60-day notification period. Greer said the administration wants both governments to take steps to meet AGOA’s criteria before the exclusions take effect.
world.image_alt: Trump moves to end AGOA duty-free access for South Africa, Rwanda

world.title: Israeli opposition backs Eisenkot as Arab parties hold balance of power
world.summary: Israeli opposition leaders are meeting Tuesday to coordinate support for former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government after an October 27 election left no bloc with a majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp won 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while Jewish-led opposition parties won 48.
world.content: Israeli opposition leaders are meeting Tuesday to coordinate support for former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government after an October 27 election left no bloc with a majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp won 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while Jewish-led opposition parties won 48. Arab-majority parties won 19, making their support potentially decisive. The opposition’s central dispute is whether to rely on Arab lawmakers. Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats, supports cooperation, while Avigdor Lieberman of Yisrael Beiteinu opposes an Arab-backed minority government. Lieberman has nevertheless said his party will recommend Eisenkot. Netanyahu is calling for a broad government under his leadership that excludes Arab parties, which he accuses of supporting terrorism and rejecting Israel’s Jewish character. President Isaac Herzog is due to receive the certified results and begin party consultations on November 4, then choose a lawmaker by November 11 to try to form a government. The nominee has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. If coalition efforts fail, further parliamentary steps could lead to a new election.
world.image_alt: Israeli opposition backs Eisenkot as Arab parties hold balance of power

world.title: US midterms open with Democrats seeking control of Congress
world.summary: Americans began voting Tuesday in midterm elections that will decide whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats take one or both chambers. Polls favor Democrats in the House, while the Senate contest remains uncertain; Democrats need a net gain of three House seats and four Senat
world.content: Americans began voting Tuesday in midterm elections that will decide whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats take one or both chambers. Polls favor Democrats in the House, while the Senate contest remains uncertain; Democrats need a net gain of three House seats and four Senate seats to win majorities. Voters have focused on the cost of living, including higher fuel prices that reports have linked to the Iran war, as well as tariffs and immigration. Democrats have pledged investigations if they win a chamber; control of the Senate would also give them power over confirmations of presidential nominees. More than 57 million people had voted early by Monday, and results may take days to become clear because states use different counting systems.
world.image_alt: US midterms open with Democrats seeking control of Congress

world.title: British adventurer Karl Bushby ends 28-year, 50,000-kilometer walk home
world.summary: Karl Bushby, a 57-year-old British former paratrooper, reached his mother’s home in Hull on Nov. 2, completing a 28-year, roughly 50,000-kilometer journey that began in southern Chile. He crossed four continents and about 30 countries, walking and swimming under self-imposed rules that barred him from using transport t
world.content: Karl Bushby, a 57-year-old British former paratrooper, reached his mother’s home in Hull on Nov. 2, completing a 28-year, roughly 50,000-kilometer journey that began in southern Chile. He crossed four continents and about 30 countries, walking and swimming under self-imposed rules that barred him from using transport to advance or returning home before finishing. The trek took far longer than Bushby’s initial estimate of about 12 years. Visa restrictions, border problems and the COVID-19 pandemic forced lengthy pauses, as did the 2008 financial crisis, which cost him sponsors. Each time, he resumed from where he had stopped. His return reunited him with his mother, whom he had not seen at home in a decade, and his adult son. He also met his 12-year-old granddaughter in person for the first time. A feature-length documentary about the expedition is in production, and Bushby plans speaking engagements in England. He has also said he is unsure what life after the journey will look like.
world.image_alt: British adventurer Karl Bushby ends 28-year, 50,000-kilometer walk home

world.title: North Korea rejects FBI claim over record $6.3 billion crypto heist
world.summary: North Korea on Tuesday denied the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s accusation that a North Korea-linked hacking unit stole more than $6.3 billion in digital assets from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange. The FBI attributed the October 29 theft to TraderTraitor, a group it associates with North Korea
world.content: North Korea on Tuesday denied the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s accusation that a North Korea-linked hacking unit stole more than $6.3 billion in digital assets from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange. The FBI attributed the October 29 theft to TraderTraitor, a group it associates with North Korean cyber activity. Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, called the allegation “absurd rhetoric” and a “grave political provocation”. Kim said Washington was unfairly linking North Korea to cybercrime worldwide and warned that Pyongyang had “issues to reconsider” over what she called U.S. hostility. Analysts in Seoul said the attribution could prompt efforts to block wallets and laundering channels that North Korea is accused of using to fund weapons programs. South Korea’s central bank estimated North Korea’s 2025 gross domestic product at 47.18 trillion won, making the alleged theft roughly one-sixth of that figure. President Donald Trump said investigators did not yet know whether North Korea was responsible. Binance said it had replaced about 95% of the stolen assets and was reopening withdrawals on additional networks starting Tuesday. The FBI urged cryptocurrency providers to block transactions linked to identified wallets.
world.image_alt: North Korea rejects FBI claim over record $6.3 billion crypto heist

business.title: Asian stocks slide as tech worries and US midterms unsettle investors
business.summary: Asian shares fell Tuesday, with South Korea’s market down as much as 4.1% and Taiwan’s benchmark losing 3.3%, as investors weighed doubts about technology-sector spending and earnings ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. The broad MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan dropped 1.4% to its lowest level since Oct. 23. Jap
business.content: Asian shares fell Tuesday, with South Korea’s market down as much as 4.1% and Taiwan’s benchmark losing 3.3%, as investors weighed doubts about technology-sector spending and earnings ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. The broad MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan dropped 1.4% to its lowest level since Oct. 23. Japan’s market was closed for a holiday. The selloff followed a 0.5% decline in the S&P 500. Investors also awaited election results that could change control of Congress and influence debates over fiscal policy, the debt ceiling and AI regulation. Reuters said investors would also watch the U.S. Treasury’s quarterly refunding announcement the next day. Oil steadied after Monday’s sharp fall, with Brent up 0.5% to $105.30 a barrel in Asian trading.
business.image_alt: Asian stocks slide as tech worries and US midterms unsettle investors

business.title: Irish low-cost airline Ryanair weighs pay freezes as fuel costs rise €2bn
business.summary: Ryanair, Europe’s largest airline by passenger numbers, is considering temporary pay freezes, smaller cabin crews and wider use of artificial intelligence as it prepares for a projected €2 billion increase in its fuel bill in the financial year starting April 2027. The airline said higher fares would not fully cover th
business.content: Ryanair, Europe’s largest airline by passenger numbers, is considering temporary pay freezes, smaller cabin crews and wider use of artificial intelligence as it prepares for a projected €2 billion increase in its fuel bill in the financial year starting April 2027. The airline said higher fares would not fully cover the added expense. Chief executive Michael O’Leary expects European short-haul fares to rise materially in 2027 as fuel prices stay high and airlines’ fuel hedges expire. Ryanair’s net profit for the six months to September fell 15% to €2.15 billion, while revenue rose 3% to €10.08 billion and passenger numbers grew 6% to 125.8 million. Average fares fell 4%. The company has hedged 80% of its fuel needs through March 2027 at about $67 a barrel, but only 25% of the following year’s needs at about $95. Ryanair has announced no cost-cutting decisions and said uncertainty made a full-year profit forecast premature.
business.image_alt: Irish low-cost airline Ryanair weighs pay freezes as fuel costs rise €2bn

business.title: U.S. gasoline prices hit Election Day record as diesel tops $6
business.summary: U.S. gasoline averaged $4.17 a gallon on Monday, putting prices on track for an Election Day record, 37 cents above the previous high of $3.80 in 2022, as voters head to the polls on Nov. 3. President Donald Trump promised during his 2024 campaign to bring gasoline prices down to $2 a gallon. Fuel costs have risen sinc
business.content: U.S. gasoline averaged $4.17 a gallon on Monday, putting prices on track for an Election Day record, 37 cents above the previous high of $3.80 in 2022, as voters head to the polls on Nov. 3. President Donald Trump promised during his 2024 campaign to bring gasoline prices down to $2 a gallon. Fuel costs have risen since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in February and Iran largely blocked oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting supply. Diesel, a key fuel for transport, agriculture and industry, has climbed about 70% during Trump’s second term to around $6.30 a gallon. The administration temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel imports. Three tankers carrying a total of about 140,000 tonnes are expected to unload at U.S. ports after the election, though energy analysts expect little near-term price relief.
business.image_alt: U.S. gasoline prices hit Election Day record as diesel tops $6

business.title: US factory activity accelerates as input costs stay elevated
business.summary: U.S. manufacturing expanded faster in October, with the Institute for Supply Management’s purchasing managers’ index rising to 55.5 from 54.5 in September, exceeding economists’ forecasts and marking a 10th straight month of growth. The production gauge climbed to 59, its highest level since November 2021, as consumer
business.content: U.S. manufacturing expanded faster in October, with the Institute for Supply Management’s purchasing managers’ index rising to 55.5 from 54.5 in September, exceeding economists’ forecasts and marking a 10th straight month of growth. The production gauge climbed to 59, its highest level since November 2021, as consumer and business demand, including investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers, supported factory output. The ISM measure of prices paid eased to 75.2 from 77.9 but remained elevated, while supplier deliveries slowed for an 11th consecutive month; manufacturers cited shortages of aluminum, copper, electronics and memory chips. Susan Spence, chair of the ISM Manufacturing Business Survey Committee, said negative sentiment worsened for a third month, with 66% of respondents’ comments negative. The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4.00% last week; economists expect inflation to remain above its 2% target into 2027.
business.image_alt: US factory activity accelerates as input costs stay elevated

business.title: European supermarket cyberattacks disrupt refrigeration and spoil food
business.summary: A Belgian Delhaize shop estimated it lost €100,000 worth of produce after hackers tampered with refrigeration controls, while a Belgian butcher put its losses from spoiled meat at about €15,000. The incidents on Nov. 2 affected refrigeration at supermarkets and other food retailers across several European countries; so
business.content: A Belgian Delhaize shop estimated it lost €100,000 worth of produce after hackers tampered with refrigeration controls, while a Belgian butcher put its losses from spoiled meat at about €15,000. The incidents on Nov. 2 affected refrigeration at supermarkets and other food retailers across several European countries; some retailers removed chilled and frozen goods, losing stock and facing cleanup work. The attack affected dozens of Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg, 15 of Carrefour’s 700 Belgian stores, five Spar franchise shops and 13 SuperValu stores in Ireland. Carrefour said it took measures to keep all its shops open; Delhaize said distribution centres and deliveries continued normally. Refrigeration equipment connected for remote monitoring and maintenance can give intruders a way to alter temperatures. Sabcobel chief executive Stephan Moelans said some affected units needed physical changes, not just software updates; he also said about 10% of Sabcobel installations remained unfixed after the October French attack. Danish manufacturer Danfoss has urged customers to disconnect systems from public internet addresses, update firmware and use network protection.
business.image_alt: European supermarket cyberattacks disrupt refrigeration and spoil food

business.title: Palantir lifts 2026 outlook as U.S. commercial sales eclipse U.S. government sales
business.summary: Palantir Technologies, the U.S. data-analytics software company, raised its 2026 revenue forecast after third-quarter revenue nearly doubled to $2.31 billion, beating analysts’ estimates. U.S. commercial revenue rose 148% to $984 million, topping U.S. government revenue of $953 million for the first time. Adjusted earn
business.content: Palantir Technologies, the U.S. data-analytics software company, raised its 2026 revenue forecast after third-quarter revenue nearly doubled to $2.31 billion, beating analysts’ estimates. U.S. commercial revenue rose 148% to $984 million, topping U.S. government revenue of $953 million for the first time. Adjusted earnings were 44 cents a share, above the 41 cents analysts expected. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $2.649 billion to $2.653 billion and raised its full-year forecast to $8.530 billion to $8.534 billion, or about 91% annual growth. Chief Executive Alex Karp has tied demand to “sovereign AI,” Palantir’s approach to deploying AI while customers retain control of sensitive data and how the technology is used. Palantir shares fell about 3% in after-hours trading after initially rising, as investors weighed high expectations and slower growth in U.S. commercial contract value. Growth in that contract value slowed to 11% year over year from more than 153% in the previous quarter.
business.image_alt: Palantir lifts 2026 outlook as U.S. commercial sales eclipse U.S. government sales

business.title: Oil prices plunge 7.6% as Iran talks ease supply fears
business.summary: Oil prices fell sharply on Monday, with Brent crude settling 7.6% lower at $104.77 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate down 7.4% to $96.46, after signs that Iran was open to continued negotiations with Washington. The declines were the benchmarks’ biggest percentage drops since July 27. Iranian President Masoud P
business.content: Oil prices fell sharply on Monday, with Brent crude settling 7.6% lower at $104.77 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate down 7.4% to $96.46, after signs that Iran was open to continued negotiations with Washington. The declines were the benchmarks’ biggest percentage drops since July 27. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had given the government authority to pursue dialogue, while Qatar mediated contacts between Tehran and Washington; no agreement had been announced. Iran has linked reopening the Strait of Hormuz to U.S. concessions, and attacks on shipping have continued. The price move reversed part of a rally driven by fears of renewed U.S. strikes after the Nov. 3 midterm elections and the risk of further disruption to Gulf oil flows. President Donald Trump had not made a decision on resuming attacks, while Israel’s prime minister urged him to strike after the vote. A follow-up meeting remained possible, but the diplomatic effort had yet to produce a breakthrough.
business.image_alt: Oil prices plunge 7.6% as Iran talks ease supply fears

business.title: Anthropic reports $17 billion in quarterly revenue, discloses $895 billion in AI commitments
business.summary: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, reported $16.96 billion in third-quarter revenue in an amended U.S. initial public offering filing on Nov. 2, while disclosing $895.4 billion in purchase and lease commitments, mostly for computing capacity and infrastructure. Revenue rose about 47% from the previous quarter,
business.content: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, reported $16.96 billion in third-quarter revenue in an amended U.S. initial public offering filing on Nov. 2, while disclosing $895.4 billion in purchase and lease commitments, mostly for computing capacity and infrastructure. Revenue rose about 47% from the previous quarter, down from 144% growth in the second quarter, and the company recorded a $23.29 billion net loss. About $69.8 billion of the commitments is due in the 12 months after Sept. 30, and roughly $447.5 billion is expected by the end of 2030. Anthropic also swung from operating income of $974 million in the second quarter to an operating loss of $567 million in the third, driven largely by $5 billion in short-term computing costs and a $2 billion non-cash donation-matching charge. Anthropic’s IPO is expected before the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday. The company cautioned that financing problems at its infrastructure partners could delay or reduce contracted capacity, or raise its cost.
business.image_alt: Anthropic reports $17 billion in quarterly revenue, discloses $895 billion in AI commitments

science.title: Turkey-sized oviraptor identified as first specialized fruit-eating dinosaur
science.summary: Paleontologists identified Infernogallus jamesi, a turkey-sized dinosaur from the Hell Creek Formation, as the first known dinosaur specialized for eating fruit. The toothless, bird-like species lived about 66 million years ago; skull analysis found adaptations for chewing soft plant foods. Researchers said some dinosa
science.content: Paleontologists identified Infernogallus jamesi, a turkey-sized dinosaur from the Hell Creek Formation, as the first known dinosaur specialized for eating fruit. The toothless, bird-like species lived about 66 million years ago; skull analysis found adaptations for chewing soft plant foods. Researchers said some dinosaurs may have dispersed the seeds of flowering plants, though that role needs further evidence. The team described the species in Nature Communications; it lived alongside animals including Tyrannosaurus rex and Triceratops.
science.image_alt: Turkey-sized oviraptor identified as first specialized fruit-eating dinosaur

science.title: Studies link industrial lifestyles and disease to gut microbial shifts
science.summary: Three studies report differences in gut microbiomes. Industrialized lifestyles were associated with less diverse, more similar bacterial communities; research on manatees mapped microbes involved in digesting aquatic plants; and an Indian study found bacterial differences in people with Parkinson’s disease. The industr
science.content: Three studies report differences in gut microbiomes. Industrialized lifestyles were associated with less diverse, more similar bacterial communities; research on manatees mapped microbes involved in digesting aquatic plants; and an Indian study found bacterial differences in people with Parkinson’s disease. The industrialization study also detected changes in microbial genomes and elevated gut inflammatory markers, though researchers said they still need to identify which changes may contribute to illness. The manatee research built a genomic atlas of freshwater and marine manatees. The Parkinson’s study compared patients with healthy participants and found more inflammation-associated bacteria and fewer bacteria that produce short-chain fatty acids. The Parkinson’s findings show an association, not proof that gut bacteria cause or drive the disease. Researchers say the findings may inform future work on early detection and gut-focused treatment.
science.image_alt: Studies link industrial lifestyles and disease to gut microbial shifts

science.title: NASA’s Swift telescope faces uncontrolled Earth reentry after rescue fails
science.summary: NASA expects its Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a 1.5-ton space telescope, to reenter Earth’s atmosphere around 3:30 a.m. Eastern time on Nov. 4, with an 11-hour uncertainty window, as its orbit decays. Most of the spacecraft should burn up, but dense components could survive. NASA puts the risk of harm to anyone on E
science.content: NASA expects its Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a 1.5-ton space telescope, to reenter Earth’s atmosphere around 3:30 a.m. Eastern time on Nov. 4, with an 11-hour uncertainty window, as its orbit decays. Most of the spacecraft should burn up, but dense components could survive. NASA puts the risk of harm to anyone on Earth at about 1 in 2,100. The U.S. Space Force is tracking the spacecraft’s path, and NASA says it will update reentry predictions. The reentry follows a failed rescue attempt by NASA and Katalyst Space Technologies: the robotic craft intended to raise Swift’s orbit lost control before reaching it. Swift operated for nearly 22 years, far beyond its planned two-year mission, and recorded more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 supernovae. Its rapid alerts helped other telescopes investigate cosmic explosions; NASA has said scientists are still working out how to fill that role.
science.image_alt: NASA’s Swift telescope faces uncontrolled Earth reentry after rescue fails

science.title: Researchers outline space sunshade concept to reduce global warming
science.summary: The Planetary Sunshade Institute, a Southern California nonprofit, says a large reflective structure in space could block about 1% of incoming sunlight and lower global temperatures by as much as 1°C. Its report describes a possible climate intervention, not a project ready for construction. Construction could begin in
science.content: The Planetary Sunshade Institute, a Southern California nonprofit, says a large reflective structure in space could block about 1% of incoming sunlight and lower global temperatures by as much as 1°C. Its report describes a possible climate intervention, not a project ready for construction. Construction could begin in 20 to 40 years if major engineering and launch hurdles are overcome. The report favors a formation of about 5,000 reflective-sail satellites over a more speculative cloud of particles. It estimates that a design intended to provide 1°C of cooling would require 70 million tons of material. A separate analysis from Carnegie Europe warns that solar-radiation modification could alter rainfall unevenly and that governance is lagging behind research.
science.image_alt: Researchers outline space sunshade concept to reduce global warming

science.title: Rubin survey reports new Neptune Trojans alongside dwarf-planet candidate
science.summary: Researchers presenting results from Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory at a planetary-science meeting described two newly identified Neptune Trojan asteroids and a third candidate, along with further details about 2026 ED138, a distant object proposed as a dwarf planet. ED138’s estimated diameter of 600 to 1,500 kilomet
science.content: Researchers presenting results from Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory at a planetary-science meeting described two newly identified Neptune Trojan asteroids and a third candidate, along with further details about 2026 ED138, a distant object proposed as a dwarf planet. ED138’s estimated diameter of 600 to 1,500 kilometers is based on its brightness and assumed reflectivity. Astronomers have not established whether it is round, a requirement for dwarf-planet classification. The Trojan findings came from the observatory’s commissioning data. The two new objects join a small group of bodies trailing Neptune and appear similar in composition to the leading Trojans, consistent with models of solar-system formation. Astronomers said Rubin’s repeated sky scans can detect objects against dense star fields, though University of Regina astronomer Sam Lawler warned that bright satellites crossing the telescope’s field may hinder future searches.
science.image_alt: Rubin survey reports new Neptune Trojans alongside dwarf-planet candidate

science.title: Sierra Club projects data centers could add 618 million tons of CO2
science.summary: A Sierra Club analysis estimates that power generation for U.S. data centers planned between 2025 and 2030 could emit 618 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, nearly matching Germany’s reported annual emissions. Those added emissions could push U.S. power-sector emissions 42% above 2025 levels by 2030, erasing reduct
science.content: A Sierra Club analysis estimates that power generation for U.S. data centers planned between 2025 and 2030 could emit 618 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, nearly matching Germany’s reported annual emissions. Those added emissions could push U.S. power-sector emissions 42% above 2025 levels by 2030, erasing reductions made since 2011, according to the analysis. About 460 million metric tons of the projected annual emissions would come from gas generators built or contracted to serve data centers off the public grid, according to the analysis. The estimate covers proposed and pending projects. An energy-policy expert said the outcome is possible but not inevitable.
science.image_alt: Sierra Club projects data centers could add 618 million tons of CO2

science.title: Study finds rising chance of 40°C heat in Nordic countries
science.summary: Finnish Meteorological Institute researchers estimate that the annual chance of temperatures reaching 40°C somewhere in Norway, Sweden or Finland was 0.53% in 2025—six times the likelihood in 1981, though still a rare event. The study, published in npj Natural Hazards on Oct. 31, says such heat should not be treated as
science.content: Finnish Meteorological Institute researchers estimate that the annual chance of temperatures reaching 40°C somewhere in Norway, Sweden or Finland was 0.53% in 2025—six times the likelihood in 1981, though still a rare event. The study, published in npj Natural Hazards on Oct. 31, says such heat should not be treated as implausible in the region. Nordic countries have historically experienced less intense heatwaves than continental Europe, and people and infrastructure are generally less adapted to extreme heat. The researchers also estimate a 10.9% annual chance that temperatures in Norway will exceed the national record under present-day climate conditions.
science.image_alt: Study finds rising chance of 40°C heat in Nordic countries

science.title: Tests find coca and alcohol in Inca child mummies, but none of the hallucinogens screened for
science.summary: Researchers analyzing hair and nails from eight Inca children sacrificed about 500 years ago found traces of coca in hair and evidence of alcohol in some children, but none of the hallucinogens they tested for. The remains came from mountain sites in Peru and Argentina and belonged to children aged 6 to 14. The finding
science.content: Researchers analyzing hair and nails from eight Inca children sacrificed about 500 years ago found traces of coca in hair and evidence of alcohol in some children, but none of the hallucinogens they tested for. The remains came from mountain sites in Peru and Argentina and belonged to children aged 6 to 14. The findings suggest the substances may have helped prepare children for the physical and emotional strain of journeys to sacrificial sites rather than induce hallucinations, said archaeologist Dagmara Socha of the University of Warsaw. Harmine, a plant compound associated with Amazonian species, was found in a nail from Juanita, a 14-year-old mummy. The team plans further study of the substances and sacred mountain sites.
science.image_alt: Tests find coca and alcohol in Inca child mummies, but none of the hallucinogens screened for

sports.title: Gerrard backs Arsenal to retain title, names three challengers
sports.summary: Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard has reiterated his prediction that Arsenal will retain the Premier League title, naming Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea as their likely challengers. sports.content: Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard has reiterated his prediction that Arsenal will retain the Premier League title, naming Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea as their likely challengers. His comments follow Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, which moved the defending champions three points clear at the top and left Liverpool nine points behind. Gerrard praised Arsenal’s ability to win through “grit and fight” rather than relying only on big scorelines, but said Liverpool still have work to do to mount a challenge. Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice also urged caution, saying the title race cannot be judged in November and teams need to keep winning into February or March. Both clubs return to Champions League action midweek, with Arsenal visiting Slavia Prague and Liverpool travelling to Fenerbahce. Arsenal then host Hull and Liverpool visit Crystal Palace in their next league matches.

sports.title: MLB names finalists as Crow-Armstrong, Misiorowski lead awards races
sports.summary: Major League Baseball and the Baseball Writers’ Association of America (BBWAA) named the top three vote-getters for 10 regular-season awards on Monday, with Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski among the leading contenders. Winners will be announced Nov. 9-12,
sports.content: Major League Baseball and the Baseball Writers’ Association of America (BBWAA) named the top three vote-getters for 10 regular-season awards on Monday, with Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski among the leading contenders. Winners will be announced Nov. 9-12, starting with Rookie of the Year. Crow-Armstrong is favored for National League Most Valuable Player after hitting 45 home runs and stealing 41 bases, becoming the seventh player in major-league history to reach 40-40. He also led the majors in FanGraphs wins above replacement (fWAR) at 10.6 and recorded a +26 fielding run value. Misiorowski, a World Series champion in his second season, led the majors with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts, making him the NL Cy Young favorite. Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez is favored for AL MVP, while rookie Parker Messick is a finalist for both AL Cy Young and Rookie of the Year. The 2026 ballot also introduces a BBWAA Reliever of the Year award in each league, separate from MLB’s existing Rivera and Hoffman honors. The Brewers have the most finalists with four: Misiorowski, second baseman Brice Turang, closer Trevor Megill and manager Pat Murphy.

sports.title: Harry Kane says he would trade Ballon d’Or for Champions League
sports.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane said Monday he would trade his 2026 Ballon d’Or for a Champions League title, speaking before Bayern’s Tuesday league-phase match against Atlético Madrid in Madrid. sports.content: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane said Monday he would trade his 2026 Ballon d’Or for a Champions League title, speaking before Bayern’s Tuesday league-phase match against Atlético Madrid in Madrid. Kane said winning with his teammates would mean more than individual recognition, though he hopes to achieve both. He became the first Englishman since 2001 to win the award, ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal. Bayern have won one of their first three league-phase matches, drawing with Arsenal and Viking, and face Atlético without head coach Vincent Kompany, who is recovering after collapsing at training. Assistant coach Aaron Danks is overseeing the team. Kane also said he is close to extending his contract, which runs until June 2027, with minor details still to resolve.

sports.title: ESPN host Michael Wilbon takes indefinite leave for health reasons
sports.summary: Michael Wilbon, the ESPN sports commentator and co-host of “Pardon the Interruption,” is taking an indefinite leave from the show and his NBA work for ESPN and ABC to address multiple health issues. sports.content: Michael Wilbon, the ESPN sports commentator and co-host of “Pardon the Interruption,” is taking an indefinite leave from the show and his NBA work for ESPN and ABC to address multiple health issues. He said he hopes to return but has no timetable. Wilbon last appeared on the show on Oct. 26; he later told his co-host, Tony Kornheiser, that he had felt “beyond exhausted” and “lifeless,” and that diabetes was part, but not all, of what he was dealing with. Wilbon said medical professionals and people close to him, including Kornheiser, had noticed warning signs in recent years and urged him to take time away sooner. ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said the network supports Wilbon and his family. ESPN will likely use guest hosts on “Pardon the Interruption” and assign other analysts to Wilbon’s NBA duties while he focuses on his health.

sports.title: Bears beat defending champion Seahawks 34-17 in Simmons’ debut
sports.summary: The Chicago Bears beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in Seattle on Monday, Nov. 2, as newly acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made his Chicago debut. Simmons had six tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss and a pass breakup, while quarterback Caleb Williams threw for 247 yards and a to
sports.content: The Chicago Bears beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in Seattle on Monday, Nov. 2, as newly acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made his Chicago debut. Simmons had six tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss and a pass breakup, while quarterback Caleb Williams threw for 247 yards and a touchdown without an interception. Running back D’Andre Swift scored three times. Chicago improved to 6-2 with its third straight victory and fifth in six games; Seattle fell to 4-4 after losing for the third time in four games. Chicago opened with a 17-play, 80-yard touchdown drive. After Seattle cut the lead from 20-9 to 20-17 in the fourth quarter, a 39-yard play by Kalif Raymond set up Swift’s second touchdown of the night. Seattle gained 252 total yards and converted one of 11 third downs; an interception off a tipped pass by Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold helped Chicago secure the win. The Bears next host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Nov. 8. Seattle finished with 81 rushing yards.

sports.title: Aston Villa drops legal threat against Jamie Carragher after apology
sports.summary: Aston Villa has dropped its threat of legal action against Sky Sports football pundit Jamie Carragher after he apologised for insulting comments about the club and its supporters. Villa threatened legal action on Friday after Carragher said on the Stick to Football podcast that manager Unai Emery would likely consider
sports.content: Aston Villa has dropped its threat of legal action against Sky Sports football pundit Jamie Carragher after he apologised for insulting comments about the club and its supporters. Villa threatened legal action on Friday after Carragher said on the Stick to Football podcast that manager Unai Emery would likely consider the Manchester United job and told Villa fans to “shut up”. He apologised on Saturday, calling his language “clumsy and wrong”. Carragher made the remarks during a discussion of whether Emery might replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. He argued that football has a hierarchy in which larger clubs can attract players and managers from smaller ones, saying Villa would never be Manchester United. Villa had threatened legal proceedings but had not formally filed a case. Emery joined Villa in 2022 and led the team to the Europa League title in 2026. Villa are due to face Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

sports.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he is focused on Tuesday’s Champions League match against Roma, with his team winless in nine games and his position under scrutiny before the November international break. United lost 2-0 at Chelsea on Saturday and are 17th in the Premier League, level on points with C
sports.content: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he is focused on Tuesday’s Champions League match against Roma, with his team winless in nine games and his position under scrutiny before the November international break. United lost 2-0 at Chelsea on Saturday and are 17th in the Premier League, level on points with Crystal Palace in the relegation zone. They are also 21st in the Champions League league phase after three matches. The top 24 teams advance from that phase. The Roma match and Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Aston Villa are United’s final fixtures before the break, when the club could review Carrick’s future. Carrick said he was not looking beyond the Roma game and defended Lisandro Martínez’s commitment after the defender’s red card at Chelsea. Martínez is available on Tuesday but suspended for the Villa match. Roma are unbeaten in Serie A after 10 games. Coach Gian Piero Gasperini says his side will treat United as a strong opponent despite their recent results. United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo urged his teammates to repay Carrick’s support with performances and results.

sports.content: Venus Williams ended her 2026 singles season without a win after losing 6-2, 6-3 to fellow American Mary Stoiana in the first round of the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Monday. The 46-year-old, ranked 597th, has now lost 17 consecutive singles matches; her last tour-level win came in July 2025. Stoiana, 23 and ranked 114th, advanced after a 77-minute match. Williams left her plans for 2027 undecided, saying she was taking things one week at a time and might ask her sister Serena what she plans to do. Her singles season is over, but she is still entered in Hong Kong doubles with Xu Yifan. Some critics argued that tournament wildcards for the former world No. 1 should go to other players.
